rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Setup 3 Game Play 4 Actions 5 End of Round Scoring 6 Final Scoring 7 Tie-breakers 8 Two-Player Rules 9 Solo Play Rules 10 Mis-click Handling Assistance Objective Earn the most victory points while exploring the country (placing tents) and finding gems. Setup Two six-sided dice per player are used. Each player starts with three pounds of coins, and eleven tents in their tent supply. The Steamboat starts on the first water space on the left side of the Gameboard. All stones (rocks and gems) are placed in the bag. Game Play Play proceeds one player at a time in rounds. At the start of each round, all dice are rolled and placed into a common supply. On their turn, a player must select one die to start their turn. If a player has previously selected a die this round, the next die selected this round must be a higher value. If a player cannot select one of the remaining dice, their turn is skipped. After taking a die, the player's turn begins and they execute one of the four Actions (see below). At any time during their turn, a player may also: donate to the Queen up to their coins in hand, sell gems in their hand at the values listed on the Gameboard, or play an Action Card. The No Cost Tent and Ignore Die Value Tent cards require an unused selected die as per the Place a Tent action. The No Cost Tent and Ignore Die Value Tent cards may be played at the same time. Sold gems are set aside. A round ends when all dice have been selected, or no players have a valid die they can select. At the end of the round, the round is scored (see below), and then the Steamboat is moved one water space to the right. The game ends when the round completes with the Steamboat in the rightmost water space. All rounds are scored, including the final round. When the game ends, final scoring occurs (see below). Actions Draw an Action Card: the player draws one Action Card from the deck and places it in their hand. If a Mine Collapse card is drawn, all gems in all players' hands are returned to the bag and the player draws another Action Card. Take Coins: the player receives coins in the number of pounds equal to their chosen die value. Dig in the Mine: the player pulls random stones out of the bag equal to their chosen die value. If a white rock is drawn, all stones pulled during the player's turn, and any set aside stones, are returned to the bag. When the last stone is pulled, any pulled gems are placed in the player's hand, and any black rocks pulled are set aside. Place a Tent: A tent is placed in the column above the Steamboat, in the row indicated on the selected die, if the player has enough coins and has a tent remaining in their tent supply. The player must pay the expedition cost indicated in the coin symbol, located just above the water space, for that column. The player must also pay one pound for any other player's tent in that space to that other player. End of Round Scoring The player receives the victory point value indicated on the left side of the row for each tent in the column above the Steamboat. Final Scoring For each of the six rows, the player with the most tents in that row receives the victory point value indicated on the right of the row. Rows with no tents in them are not scored. If players tie for the most number of tents in the row, the victory points for that row are divided equally, rounded down. Each player receives one victory point for each gem in their hand. Each player scores any victory point Action Cards in their hand. Once all victory points are awarded, each player's donations to the Queen are revealed. The player with the lowest donation is disqualified from the game (score is set to zero). If players tie for lowest donation, all of those players are disqualified. Tie-breakers In case of a victory point tie, the player with the largest donation is the winner. In case of a victory point and donation tie, the player with the most placed tents is the winner. Two-Player Rules When a player's tent supply runs out, they may move an existing tent on the board when placing a tent, including a free tent. At the end of the game, four dice are rolled, and the sum of those dice is the minimum donation amount a player must have donated to avoid being disqualified. Solo Play Rules Overall goal is to maximize victory points, 50 or better is a good score. Two action die are used per round. Between 15 to 20 "white" tents are randomly placed across the board at the start of the game. White tents increase expedition cost to place a tent in those locations, and affect final row scoring, as if they belonged to another player. No other changes to round play or final scoring. Two dice are rolled at the end of the game, and the player's donations must exceed that value to avoid disqualification. Mis-click Handling Assistance The Livingstone interface provides the following assistance to players to help prevent and/or recover from a single mis-click. The player is provided the option to Undo their last take coins (not via a card), donation, gem sale (not in market) or placed tent (not via a card). It takes clicking twice on the draw deck or an action card in the player's hand to take that action. Digging in the mine (not via a card) can be cancelled, if that is done before the first stone is drawn out of the bag.

---

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] The rulebook outright contradicts itself, sometimes in the same paragraph, and looking through the rules in the original German only creates more questions than it answers. This game is simply incomplete.

[Rating: 2/10] We wanted to leave the game on the table halfway through, but we didn't, just because we respect games... It's beautiful, but I don't think, I would ever play it again.

[Rating: 2/10] I did not enjoy this game at all. I drew the white gem 3 times and finished so far in last because I was never able to do anything.

[Rating: 3/10] Didn't like it right from the explanation of rules, a mixture of several luck-dependent components. Great: Each player is Livingstone (a scot), the player that donates the least gold to the Queen loses regardless of accumulated victory points. I guess, Livingstone would have chosen this loser as best incarnation of himself ...

[Rating: 3/10] It's not so bad that I wouldn't play again, but Livingstone is a mish mash of game mechanisms which seem like there weren't playtested in order to balance the game.  I can definitely see what was trying to be done here, but nothing actually works the way it was intended to work.  It seems like the first prototype of a game that needed to be playtested a lot more in order to realize its potential.  As is, it's a rather unbalanced mess of a game.

[Rating: 3/10] The excellent dice-mechanic shines as one very lonely star in this mess of unrelated mechanics with no interconnecting narrative and /way/ to much luck-dependance.  Spielbox was to kind in it's review.  ... and what's with the river running the wrong way???

[Rating: 3/10] Nem egy nagy durranás. Bemelegítő játéknak jó lenne, ha nem lenne hosszabb, mint 15 perc. Egyik kártya jelentése kapcsán vita volt.

[Rating: 3/10] The great art, theme, and some mechanics tricked me into thinking this would be a fun game. It's just putting tents on a grid.

[Rating: 3/10] Luck in the dice rolling, luck in the card drawing, and more luck in the gem pulling. A bit too long for this much luck.

[Rating: 3/10] Very simple family-style euro. A chaotic push-your-luck element that will frustrate many, but it works for me.

[Rating: 3/10] Drawing the gems from a bag is obviously lucky but the game knows and owns it. It's not bad just too simple for a gamer and it's not going to appeal to kids.

[Rating: 3.5/10] Too much luck even for a light and quick family game. The dice mechanic seems clever at first glance, but in practice it really plays itself. There are some agonizing choices in what to do with them, but which die to select is usually obvious. The best thing about the game is the artwork by Michael Menzel.

[Rating: 3.5/10] In a game that is far too long for its own good, the inclusion of cards that can actually extend the number of game turns is a terrible idea.  Livingstone also has "draw from the bag" randomness (in the vein of Thebes) that is knee-slapping fun when someone gets burned, but isn't good for much else.

[Rating: 4/10] Too random: - Value of the cards can be quite different. - Drawing gems gives you on average 1.1 money per draw - but we had somebody pulling out 18 money with 5 dice, another player 0. Usually, you need to spend an action to get 4-6 gold.  The treasure chects are very beautiful made, and completely useless. There is no point at all to put in any money until the last turn.  Rating further downgraded after more plays

[Rating: 4/10] Extremely random and too long, but nice components.  Furthermore, completely unfun if you play it with serious gamers. There are a lot of actions (for example putting money in your chest) which don' make sense until the last turn.  however, I admit that it may be  hit with your family.

[Rating: 4/10] First impression (3 players): After reading the rules game felt ok but it soon turned out to be rather silly. Dice mechanic is pretty clever and is the best part of the game. With just 3 players the rule that one who donated least will lose is quite harsh. On the other hand with 4+ players this will be most likely too chaotic. Endgame is silly as you may hoard cards and then play many of them in sequence. There are some killer combinations that can literally win you the game at the last turn(s). As a final insult the score marker is too big for the score track!

[Rating: 4/10] Interesting theme and cool components. Game incorporates mechanisms from different games known to general gaming public in an interesting way. I liked the dice and didn't like the use two dice card (which is very strong) and the white stone in the bag (can basically ruin your game if you happen to be unlucky).  EDIT: The rule of the white gem is really unclear in the Finnish rules but after resolving the problem with the help of BGG community (you are able to sell the stones you draw on your turn before they go into the bag) the game is much better.

[Rating: 4/10] A mish mash of mechanics makes up a mildly interesting family fare. With three players it seems there's all too much of actions, money and points. This game would have benefited from special set-up for different number of players rather to make it tighter than having for example a chest for surplus money.

[Rating: 4/10] Even our second game, when everybody knew the rules, took over an hour and half, and that is too much for a game like this. 30 to 45 minutes as the box said would be quite right, but I don't know how it can be done. The game itself appears to be quite simple, there are some cards to give more options and the amount of dice give a nice touch of randomess, but still there is something, that I just don't get. Not a game for me, too long and too boring.
